_meta.description: Drill items for FretPath Tier 0-2 foundation nodes (N01-N12). Drop-in seed matching the Item model in the build spec. Standard tuning unless metadata says otherwise: strings 6=low E, 5=A, 4=D, 3=G, 2=B, 1=high e. Grades are self-rated 0-5; each item's metadata.selfAssess tells the user what a 5 feels like.
_meta.itemModel: Item { id, nodeId, type, prompt, answer, difficulty(1-10), metadata }

items.prompt: Sit with the guitar on your leg, fretting wrist relaxed and low. Hold the pick between your thumb and the side of your index finger. Play 8 slow downstrokes on the open low E (6th) string.
items.answer: 8 even, ringing downstrokes with a relaxed hand.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = every note rings clearly, hand stays loose, no gripping tension.

items.prompt: Pick-angle drill: play the open A (5th) string 8 times, angling the pick roughly 20 degrees so it glides across the string instead of catching flat.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = pick glides smoothly, consistent volume, no scratchy catches.

items.prompt: Chromatic climb on the low E: frets 1-2-3-4, one finger per fret (fingers 1-2-3-4), tight and even. This is the riff engine behind half of thrash, Slayer to early Metallica.
items.answer: A four-note chromatic run F-F#-G-G#, one finger per fret.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = each note clean and buzz-free, evenly spaced, fingertips landing just behind the fret.

items.prompt: Descending chromatic lick on the high e string: frets 4-3-2-1 (fingers 4-3-2-1), even and controlled. Play it like a lead fill, not a warm-up.
items.answer: A four-note descending chromatic lick G#-G-F#-F.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = clean tone on the thin string, no muting from neighbouring fingers, evenly timed.

items.prompt: Finger independence: fret the 3rd string at fret 5 with your 3rd finger only, other fingers hovering close, and pluck it 4 times cleanly.
items.answer: Note C, played cleanly with the 3rd finger.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = clean C each time with the other fingers relaxed and off the strings.

items.prompt: In guitar tab, the number '3' written on the TOP line (thinnest string) means which string and which fret?
items.answer: 1st string (high e), 3rd fret = the note G.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = answered from memory without checking.

items.prompt: Read this tab fragment on the high e string:  e|--0--3--|  Name the two notes in order.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = named both correctly.

items.prompt: In a chord diagram, what does a number printed just below a string (at the bottom) usually tell you?
items.answer: Which fretting finger to use for that note (1=index, 2=middle, 3=ring, 4=pinky).

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = knew it without hesitation.

items.prompt: Set a metronome to 60 bpm. Play ONE downstroke on the open low E exactly on each click, for 16 clicks. Lock every note to the beat.
items.answer: 16 quarter notes perfectly on the click.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = you can't hear the click because your note lands right on top of it.

items.prompt: At 60 bpm, play TWO evenly spaced notes per click (eighth notes) on the open A string for 16 clicks.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = both notes evenly spaced, second note landing exactly halfway between clicks.

items.prompt: At 80 bpm, play steady quarter notes on the open D string for 16 clicks without drifting ahead of or behind the beat.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = rock-steady, no rushing or dragging.

items.prompt: Play a G5 power chord: root on the 6th string fret 3 (G) plus the 5th string fret 5. Strum ONLY those two strings, cleanly, muting the rest.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = both notes ring, no other strings sounding.

items.prompt: Play an A5 power chord: 5th string open (A) plus 4th string fret 2. Mute everything else.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = clean two-note chord, no ringing 6th string.

items.prompt: Power chords are movable. For a C5 with its root on the 6th string, which fret is the root on?
items.answer: 6th string fret 8 (C), with the 5th string fret 10 as the fifth.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = located it from knowing the 6th-string note names.

items.prompt: Change cleanly between G5 (6th fret 3) and C5 (6th fret 8), keeping the same shape and sliding, 4 times back and forth.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = no gap or buzz during the shift, both chords land clean.

items.prompt: Rest the side of your picking-hand palm lightly on the strings right where they meet the bridge. Play the open low E with the palm mute engaged: aim for a tight, thudding 'chug', not a ringing note. 8 downstrokes.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = short, punchy thud with pitch still audible; not fully dead, not ringing open.

items.prompt: Palm-mute a G5 power chord and play 8 even downstrokes, keeping the mute consistent.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = every chug equally tight, palm pressure steady.

items.prompt: Contrast drill on the low E: play 2 palm-muted notes, then 2 open (unmuted) notes, and repeat for 4 groups. Feel your palm lift and settle.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = obvious difference between the tight muted notes and the ringing open ones, timing even.

items.prompt: At 60 bpm, play the open low E using STRICT alternate picking (down-up-down-up). Start one note per click, then move to two per click (eighth notes).
items.answer: Even down-up eighth notes at 60 bpm.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = up-strokes as strong and even as down-strokes.

items.prompt: Alternate-pick the notes at frets 5-6-7-8 on the 6th string (one finger per fret), down-up-down-up, as eighth notes at 60 bpm.
items.answer: A, A#, B, C alternate-picked evenly.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = fretting and picking hands perfectly in sync, no flams.

items.prompt: Alternate pick ACROSS two strings: open 6th string then open 5th string, down-up, at 70 bpm eighth notes.
items.answer: Clean string crossing with strict alternate picking.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = smooth crossing, no accidental extra string noise.

items.prompt: All DOWNSTROKES (no up-strokes) on a palm-muted low E: 8 eighth notes at 80 bpm. This is the core metal rhythm-picking motion.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = consistent attack and spacing despite using only downstrokes; forearm stays relaxed.

items.prompt: Downpicked G5 chugs: all downstrokes, quarter notes at 80 bpm, for 16 beats.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = even, punchy, no fatigue creeping in.

items.prompt: Downpicked riff: alternate 3x palm-muted open low E, then 1x G5, all downstrokes, at 80 bpm. Repeat for 4 bars.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = the chord accents stay in time and the whole thing grooves.

items.prompt: Octave shape (6th-4th strings): root on 6th string fret 5 (A), octave on 4th string fret 7 (A). Fret both with the 5th string muted in between, and pluck so both A's ring together.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = both notes ring, the muted middle string stays silent.

items.prompt: Slide that same 6th-4th octave shape up so the root sits on the 6th string fret 8. What note are you now playing (in both octaves)?

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = named it from the 6th-string note map.

items.prompt: Octave shape on the 5th-3rd strings: root on 5th string fret 3 (C), octave on 3rd string fret 5 (C). Mute the 4th string between them and play cleanly.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = clean two-note octave, middle string silent.

items.prompt: A minor pentatonic, position 1 (root = 6th string fret 5). Play it ASCENDING, two notes per string:  6th(5,8)  5th(5,7)  4th(5,7)  3rd(5,7)  2nd(5,8)  1st(5,8).
items.answer: A C D E G A C D E G A C (ascending through the box).

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = every note even in volume and timing, no buzzes.

items.prompt: Play the same A minor pentatonic position 1 box DESCENDING, from the high e string back down to the low E.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = as smooth descending as ascending.

items.prompt: Name the five notes of the A minor pentatonic scale, in order.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = recalled all five from memory.

items.prompt: Play A minor pentatonic position 1 ascending at 70 bpm, strict alternate picking, two notes per click.
items.answer: The box, alternate-picked at 70 bpm eighth notes.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = locked to the click with clean down-up picking throughout.

items.prompt: Tune your 6th string DOWN a whole step (from E). Play the open 6th string now — what note is it?

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = tuned accurately to D and knew the answer.

items.prompt: In Drop D, power chords on the 6th-5th-4th strings can be barred with ONE finger. Barre the open strings (D5), then barre fret 3 (F5). Play both.
items.answer: One-finger D5 (open) and F5 (fret 3) across strings 6-5-4.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = all three strings ring under the single barred finger.

items.prompt: In Drop D, play a one-finger palm-muted riff: D5 (open) -> G5 (fret 5) -> F5 (fret 3), palm-muted, at 90 bpm. Repeat 4 times.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = tight mute, clean shifts, steady groove.

items.prompt: Core chug: palm-muted open low E, ALL downstrokes, straight eighth notes at 90 bpm, held for 2 bars (16 notes). Keep it tight and machine-even.
items.answer: 16 even palm-muted downpicked eighth notes at 90 bpm.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = perfectly even, tight mute, no tempo drift across the 2 bars.

items.prompt: Single-note riff: 8x palm-muted open low E, then 1 open G5 accent (let it ring), then repeat. 90 bpm.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = chugs stay tight and the accent pops out clearly in time.

items.prompt: Chugging with rests: play mute - mute - REST - mute on the low E (a syncopated pattern), 4 bars at 90 bpm. Practise clean starts and dead stops.
items.answer: Syncopated chug pattern with clean rests.

metadata.selfAssess: 5 = the rests are truly silent (palm kills the string) and the pattern stays locked to the beat.
